subject: Re: Helionix - request for priority latency corridor and uptime commitments
messages:
From: Sophie Greene <sophie@helionix.com>
To: hiro_tanaka@redwood.com
Date: 2028-09-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: priority latency corridor for Helionix production

Hi Hiro,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — the early results look promising. Helionix is preparing to go live with an inference-heavy feature in Q4 and our leadership has asked for a narrow latency commitment during our peak window to support a premium tier for enterprise customers.

Concrete ask: can Redwood commit to a "priority latency corridor" for Helionix where p95 inference latency is <= 75ms for requests routed to the priority pool during 6am–8pm PT, with an uptime guarantee of 99.95% for that pool across the month? We'd expect Redwood to keep a reserved pool (or equivalent routing guarantees) and provide a fallback policy when capacity is exhausted.

Attached is a short one-pager with traffic profile and expected Q4 volume. We know this is outside standard terms — looking for internal approval path, expected cost uplift, and any operational runbook requirements. Sophie

Attachment: helionix_latency_request_20280901.pdf

From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: ops-team@redwood.com
Date: 2028-09-01T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Helionix - priority latency corridor (need feasibility & numbers)

Team — forwarding Helionix's ask. TL;DR: p95 <= 75ms during 6am–8pm PT, 99.95% monthly uptime for the priority pool, reserved capacity or routing guarantees, plus a clear fallback when we have pressure.

Questions I need answered by end of day Friday:
- Feasibility: can runtime + routing guarantee a p95 <=75ms at their projected QPS with dedicated pool vs prioritized routing?
- Cost: ballpark delta vs standard hosted (preferred: per-month reserved capacity + committed throughput or a markup on per-token).
- Operational asks: what does ops need (runbook, on-call escalation, capacity prewarming)?
- Risk/fallback: recommended automatic fallback policy and expected user-visible degradation.

Karthik — can you draft a short commercial proposal and flag any deal constraints?
Marissa — can you assess the engineering feasibility and list required implementation/ops work (and an estimate in engineer-weeks)?
Laura — this will likely need a one-off SLA carve (legal + CS); can you advise on standard wording to start with and whether we can reuse the Helionix clause we did for another priority customer?

I'll consolidate and respond to Sophie with next steps.

Thanks,
Hiro
Product Partnerships | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: hiro_tanaka@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2028-09-02T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Helionix - priority latency corridor (commercial sketch)

Hi Hiro — quick commercial sketch based on Helionix's traffic doc:

Option A (Reserved Pool):
- Dedicated reserved capacity (N GPUs) sized to cover 95% of expected peak traffic; p95 target 75ms achievable with appropriate model variant and autoscale headroom.
- Pricing: fixed monthly fee for reserved capacity + nominal per-token usage.
- Commitment: 12 month minimum recommended.

Option B (Priority Routing):
- No hard reservation; priority routing with prefixed burst capacity. Lower cost but higher risk; during extreme load we must failover to standard routing with a degraded p95 (~150–200ms).

Estimate: uplift ~3.5–6x vs hosted on-demand unit economics depending on reservation size. I'll formalize with numbers once engineering confirms sizing.

Risk items to call out for Helionix: cold-starts for large models, KV cache warming across scaled nodes, cross-tenant noisy neighbor impact. Recommend we explicitly define fallback behavior (route to standard model variant + user-visible banner) and a compensation model if we miss the priority corridor more than once per quarter.

I'll draft a short proposal doc (attaching helionix_sla_draft_v1.docx) and a pricing worksheet tomorrow.

—Karthik
Account Exec, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: hiro_tanaka@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: ops-team@redwood.com, infra@redwood.com
Date: 2028-09-02T11:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Helionix - priority latency corridor (engineering ops input)

Hi all — engineering readout below. Short answer: feasible with constraints. Longer:

Implementation sketch:
- Dedicated pool preferred for deterministic p95 <=75ms. Requires reserved nodes sized for peak tail (engineer estimate: 4–6 engineer-weeks to implement the routing + pooling controls and build a limited admin UI for Helionix tenancy).
- If we go priority routing (no reservation), we can get close during normal load but will see p95 regress to ~150–200ms under sustained spikes.

Operational requirements:
- Prewarming and KV-cache warming playbook (attached runbook).
- Nightly health checks, token-level tracing for Helionix routes, and enhanced alerts for elevated queue length.
- Ops will want on-call cost visibility and an SLA incident playbook (OPS-1427).

Fallback policy (recommended):
1) When queue depth or scheduling latency breaches threshold, begin controlled degradation: route new requests to a smaller model variant with degraded quality but stable latency.
2) If degradation exceeds 2 minutes, disable priority routing and route all Helionix requests through standard pool with a user-visible status message.
3) Post-incident: automatic rollback to priority pool after cache-warm period + explicit ops sign-off.

I attached a short operational-runbook-priority-corridor.md with checklist items. If Sales wants a contractual uptime number for the priority pool, we need to agree on a reserved sizing buffer and compensation terms for misses.

Happy to sync for 30 mins if we need to walk through tradeoffs.

Marissa
Head of Product — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
Attachment: operational-runbook-priority-corridor.md

From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Greene <sophie@helionix.com>, Daniel Cruz <daniel.cruz@helionix.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, legal@helionix.com
Date: 2028-09-03T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Helionix - request for priority latency corridor and uptime commitments

Hi Sophie / Daniel — thanks for sending the request and traffic profile. Quick update and next steps: 

1) Feasibility: engineering confirms a dedicated reserved pool is the most reliable way to meet p95 <= 75ms for the expected Q4 volume. Priority routing (no reservation) is lower cost but not deterministic at tail.

2) Commercial path: Karthik will send a formal proposal with two options (Reserved Pool vs Priority Routing) and clear pricing/commitment tradeoffs. We expect uplift of 3.5–6x vs on-demand for the reserved option — final numbers in proposal.

3) Ops/runbook: Marissa's team produced a short runbook and a fallback policy. We'll include those runbook items in the operational annex to the SLA (prewarm requirements, KV cache warming, alerting, incident sequence).

4) Legal/contract: Laura — can you review helionix_sla_draft_v1.docx and advise on redlines for uptime language and compensation? Sophie / Helionix Legal — I'll share a DocuSign template once we have the option chosen.

Next steps for Helionix: please confirm whether you prefer the deterministic reserved pool (recommended) or to start with priority routing as a pilot. If you pick reserved pool, Karthik will include recommended pool size and monthly cost in the formal proposal.

DocuSign template (placeholder): https://app.docusign.com/templates/RED-HEL-PRIORITY-2028
Internal ops ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-1427

Best,
Hiro
